key_claims: A single giant AI-generated PR just sits there, reviewers lose context and feedback quality drops; it becomes slower to merge. Stacking makes changes small enough to hold in a reviewer's head. The post demonstrates teaching coding agents to build a shopping-assistant feature as an ordered four-layer stack: L1 feat/catalog-data (data modeler agent: typed catalog, seed data, validation, data access), L2 feat/search-api (backend agent, /api/products/search), L3 feat/chat-grounding (frontend agent, chat calls API), L4 feat/grounded-ui (frontend agent, product citation cards). Rebasing after a fix to the bottom layer is the hard part: GitHub offers a one-click 'Rebase stack' button (server-side, resets committer, unsigned commits, may break signed-commit branch protection) and recommends local `gh stack rebase` then `gh stack push`; `gh stack sync` fetches, cascades rebases, pushes and syncs PR state. Docs add that merging the bottom PR auto-rebases the rest.
headline_figures: 1,721 lines changed: confirmed as the figure in the post's illustrative reviewer aside (post also says '1,000+ line diff' and '1,720+ line-sized pull request' elsewhere, and a GIF growing past 1,500 lines). Lead says 1,721-line shopping-assistant PR split into four layers: matches. 400-line or 10-file threshold: NOT in the post, and docs give no numeric limit (only 'when the current branch is already large enough to review'); that lead is unsupported. Gartner projection of 50% productivity gain across every SDLC stage by 2028 appears in the intro; it is about AI in general, not stacked PRs, and was not opened at Gartner [uncertain].
sample_and_method: No sample, no method. The 1,721-line PR is a constructed demo, not a measured case. No review times, defect rates, merge statistics or customer data. Outcome: guidance only, no measured outcome exists in the post or the docs page.
limitations: Vendor guidance with no measurement. Review-quality claims ('feedback quality drops', 'faster to review') are asserted, not evidenced or cited. Stacks must be in one repo (no cross-fork), merge bottom-up, not supported in GitHub Desktop (per search snippet of Enterprise docs [uncertain]). Server-side rebase has signing caveats. Stacking addresses diff size and context, not the cost of reviewer attention or whether the agent's design is right; it can still produce four large reviews. Fetched content was model-summarised.
what_a_leader_can_do: Set a norm that agent output arrives as small ordered layers, each with its own description, and adopt tooling that removes rebase cost (gh-stack, which GitHub also ships as an agent skill). Evidence strength: weak. It is a plausible, vendor-supported practice with no measured effect on review quality or throughput, and no size threshold to adopt from this source.
overlap_with_site_essays: Light overlap with The Verification Gap and Overseeing Agents Is the Tiring Part (review load from agent-generated volume). Little overlap with Checking Isn't Catching or What It Takes to Trust Agent Output, since the post is about structuring diffs, not whether review actually catches defects. Useful as a counterpoint: a vendor remedy for size, with no evidence it improves catching.
